DISPUTE_ANSWERED:bcfa40577b48d12a.explanation: On 2026-11-20 PayPal sent a CUSTOMER.DISPUTE.CREATED event for dispute PP-D-42809: a $12.00 USD claim where the buyer says "My first bag of coffee never arrived." Your app replied 200 (meaning "received") but never sent PayPal a response before the 2026-12-10 deadline. When the seller stays silent, PayPal rules for the customer, so you lose the $12.00 and get a dispute on your record even if the coffee was actually delivered. The trace also shows verifyCalled: false, meaning your app never checked that this webhook really came from PayPal.
DISPUTE_ANSWERED:bcfa40577b48d12a.fix: In your CUSTOMER.DISPUTE.CREATED handler, save the dispute with its seller_response_due_date and alert someone (or start an automated flow) to answer it through PayPal's disputes API before that date, for example by providing tracking or delivery proof, offering a refund, or accepting the claim. Also verify each webhook's signature with PayPal before acting on it.

FULFIL_ONCE:62d64bafeaf2b03c.explanation: PayPal's simulator sent the same payment-completed notice (event WH-VGZDZD0XSESQGHOA7-SOVM92N6POBYU43VO, sale AK0DAUU2SYKTT1TA7 for $12.00 USD) twice, at 00:08 and 00:09 on 2026-11-01, and your app answered 200 both times and delivered Maya's purchase twice. Only one payment actually completed, so the business gave away a second $12.00 worth of goods or service for free. PayPal can legitimately resend the same notice, for example after a network hiccup, so this will happen in production too.
FULFIL_ONCE:62d64bafeaf2b03c.fix: Before fulfilling, record the event id (or the sale id AK0DAUU2SYKTT1TA7) in a table with a unique constraint, and skip fulfilment if that id has already been processed, while still returning 200. Do the check and the fulfilment in one database transaction so two near-simultaneous deliveries can't both slip through.

FULFIL_ONCE:645818d33faf934d.explanation: PayPal sent each completed $12.00 payment notice twice: WH-VGZDZD0XSESQGHOA7-SOVM92N6POBYU43VO was delivered at 00:08 and again at 00:09 on 2026-11-01, and WH-7UX8J0FWA36G68IUF-AOBCC5POPV1ZKXB03 at 00:07 and again at 00:13 on 2026-12-01. Your app answered 200 to all four deliveries and fulfilled each one, so Maya was given what they paid for 4 times while only 2 payments had completed. Every duplicate delivery gives away product or service for free, and PayPal can resend a notice at any time, so this keeps happening.
FULFIL_ONCE:645818d33faf934d.fix: Before fulfilling, record the event id (or the sale id, such as AK0DAUU2SYKTT1TA7) in a table with a unique constraint. If that id is already there, return 200 without fulfilling again.

FULFIL_ONCE:d2c768ab68d8d18c.explanation: PayPal's simulator sent the payment-completed notice (a webhook, an automatic message from PayPal) for the $12.00 sale ZSS6P7VTXVTKERTHS twice: event WH-4Z5IRQO86U8937LW0-0BK3YK1IYKQ2Y8Q9A arrived at 01:25 and again at 01:35 on 2026-12-01, each time with a different transmission id. Your app answered 200 both times and fulfilled the order both times, so Ana received what they paid for 3 times while only 2 payments had completed. Every duplicate notice handled this way gives away product for free, and PayPal is allowed to resend notices.
FULFIL_ONCE:d2c768ab68d8d18c.fix: Before fulfilling, save the event id (or the sale id, here ZSS6P7VTXVTKERTHS) in a table with a unique constraint. If it is already there, return 200 without fulfilling again. Do not use the transmission id for this, because it changes on every resend.

VERIFIES_SIGNATURES:3460f425f58502e8.explanation: PayPal's simulator sent the BILLING.SUBSCRIPTION.ACTIVATED notice WH-SNTW10K7WW9VEOK5F-UAUUYQ5M7UCN1XYD2 for subscription I-6IGYNTND8W9G (Ana's $12.00/month Coffee Club Monthly plan), and your app answered 200 without ever calling PayPal's signature check (verifyCalled: false). The signature is what proves a webhook really came from PayPal, so skipping it means anyone who finds your webhook URL could post a fake 'subscription activated' notice and get the plan without paying.
VERIFIES_SIGNATURES:3460f425f58502e8.fix: Before acting on any webhook, call PayPal's verify-webhook-signature API using the PayPal transmission headers and your webhook ID. Reject the request with a non-2xx status unless PayPal reports the signature as valid.

VERIFIES_SIGNATURES:c6b6497eee30e152.explanation: PayPal's simulator sent the BILLING.SUBSCRIPTION.CREATED notice WH-66AEHW6MLQIO72G4V-L3LMI8N2SREWCEPOE for Maya's Coffee Club Monthly subscription (I-LTI2N0RM0HIM), and your app answered 200 in 4 ms without ever calling PayPal's signature verification (verifyCalled: false). This one happened to be genuine, but because your app never checks, anyone who finds your webhook URL could post a fake notice and your app would trust it. An attacker could use that to unlock subscriptions nobody paid for or to change customers' records.
VERIFIES_SIGNATURES:c6b6497eee30e152.fix: Before acting on any webhook, verify it came from PayPal by sending its signature headers (PAYPAL-TRANSMISSION-ID, PAYPAL-TRANSMISSION-SIG, PAYPAL-CERT-URL, PAYPAL-AUTH-ALGO, PAYPAL-TRANSMISSION-TIME) plus your webhook ID and the event body to PayPal's /v1/notifications/verify-webhook-signature endpoint. Only process the event if the response says SUCCESS, and otherwise reject it with a non-200 status.

VERIFIES_SIGNATURES:dc1389f84ef35297.explanation: PayPal's simulator sent the PAYMENT.SALE.COMPLETED notice WH-VGZDZD0XSESQGHOA7-SOVM92N6POBYU43VO (a $12.00 USD payment on subscription I-LTI2N0RM0HIM). Your app answered 200 ("OK, processed") both times it arrived, and never checked the signature that proves the message really came from PayPal (verifyCalled is false). Without that check, anyone who knows your webhook URL could send a fake "payment completed" notice and get paid access without paying.
VERIFIES_SIGNATURES:dc1389f84ef35297.fix: Before acting on any webhook, verify it using the PayPal-Transmission-* headers PayPal sends with each delivery: call PayPal's verify-webhook-signature API with those headers, your webhook ID and the raw request body. Reject the request (for example with a 400) unless the result is SUCCESS.
